newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CHELSEA STAGE COMEBACK TO BEAT LIVERPOOL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHELSEA STAGE COMEBACK TO BEAT LIVERPOOL.

text.p: Chelsea staged an outstanding comeback in one of the most remarkable matches of the season to beat Liverpool 4-2 in the fourth round of the F.A. Cup on Sunday after trailing 2-0 at half-time.

Liverpool, driven by an inspirational display by Steve McManaman, dominated the first half and deserved to be winning with goals from Robbie Fowler after ten minutes and Stan Collymore who scored after a mix-up in the Chelsea midfield 11 minutes later.

But a tactical half-time substitution by Chelsea player-manager Ruud Gullit, who brought on the surprisingly-omitted Mark Hughes for Scott Minto, transformed the match and gave Chelsea a famous victory against last season's beaten cup finalists.

Hughes, who has a long history of playing well against Liverpool, halved the deficit within five minutes of coming on when his shot on the turn into the bottom corner gave Liverpool goalkeeper David James no chance.
Chelsea pulled level after 58 minutes when Gianfranco Zola, who had a quiet first half but an outstanding second one, beat James with a trademark curling left-foot shot from the edge of the box.

Five minutes later Chelsea were ahead when fellow Italian Gianluca Vialli, back in the side after failing to start the last eight matches, scored easily after being put through by Romanian Dan Petrescu. Vialli added the fourth from a Zola freekick after Czech Patrick Berger, who had just come on as a substitute, fouled the former Juventus captain.
Both sides attacked for almost the entire 90 minutes and the match truly was one of two differing halves which could easily have produced at least another six goals.
The match gave Chelsea revenge for their 5-1 defeat at Anfield earlier in the season, and followed their 1-0 league win over Liverpool at Stamford Bridge on New Year's Day.
Liverpool's day was summed up in the dying minutes when Fowler looked as though he had scored with a header but Chelsea keeper Kevin Hitchock pulled off a great save.
